forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved YES. Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif announced June 12 that US and Iran had reached agreement on the final MOU text; the MOU was digitally signed June 14 by named US and Iranian representatives via Pakistan mediation, before the EOD June 16 deadline. VP Vance confirmed June 15. The June 14 digital signing satisfies the criterion of a publicly confirmed held session between named US and Iranian principals via mediation, or official Iranian statement rescinds the June 1 suspension. p=0.85 reflects high but not absolute certainty due to ambiguity over whether the digital signing constitutes a 'held negotiating session' vs. the June 17 formal signing.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed convened US-Iran negotiating session occur before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved YES. US and Iranian negotiating teams held a formally convened session at Burgenstock, Switzerland, June 21-22. Named US principal VP JD Vance was present alongside Iran's chief negotiator Kazem Gharibabadi, hosted by Pakistan and Qatar as named mediators. The session produced a joint Qatar-Pakistan statement announcing a 60-day roadmap toward a final deal, Iran's commitment to invite IAEA inspectors, and a direct US-Iran Hormuz communication channel. Two independent TIER1 sources (Al Jazeera, Bloomberg) confirmed the session. The face-to-face branch of the criteria is satisfied by direct US-Iran official presence at the same venue.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar), between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Al Jazeera/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Mere relay of written messages, or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: TIER1 report of a convened session
Iran MFA statement lifting the June 1 suspension

forecasts.question: Will a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange (strikes both ways) occur in any 48h window before EOD 2026-06-24?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved NO. The MOU negotiation (June 12-17) and Burgenstock talks (June 21-22) created a bilateral diplomatic hold on direct state-to-state attacks during the June 10-24 window. IDF conducted strikes in the Beirut area on June 14 targeting Lebanese territory, not Iranian territory, and the US intervened to prevent Iranian retaliation in order to protect the MOU timeline. No confirmed direct Israeli strikes on Iranian territory AND Iranian strikes on Israeli-claimed territory within any 48h rolling window between June 10 and June 24 were found in TIER1 reporting. The June 14 Beirut incident resolves as one-directional per the ambiguity rule: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Calibration note: p=0.55 prior was directionally low for a wartime pair; the diplomatic track created an exception.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Proxy-only attacks (Hezbollah/Houthi) without direct Iran-Israel state strikes do NOT count; one-directional strikes within the 48h window = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IDF + IRGC reciprocal strike statements within 48h
TIER1 confirmation of two-way strikes in a single window

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved NO. IMF PortWatch data shows peak Hormuz commercial transit reached approximately 25 vessels/day (7-day avg) in late June following the MOU — well below the 50/day threshold. After the ceasefire collapsed July 7, transit fell to approximately 10/day (July 13-19 week), with the July 19 reading at 15 vessels/day (17% of pre-crisis baseline). The 50-vessel threshold was never reached within any consecutive 7-day window before the July 2 horizon.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

indicators.name: PortWatch 7-day transit trend rising

forecasts.question: Will mine-countermeasure clearing operations actively commence in Hormuz before EOD 2026-07-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved YES. CENTCOM formally commenced Strait of Hormuz MCM clearing operations April 11, 2026, with USS Frank E. Petersen Jr. (DDG-121) and USS Michael Murphy (DDG-112). A second operational phase commenced June 16 — one day after the MOU signing — under the framework of Operation Project Freedom, with France, UK, Germany, Italy, Japan, and Canada participating. The June 16 phase is documented as a fresh commencement within the June 10-July 10 window. Multiple TIER1 sources confirmed active in-water operations.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports mine-countermeasure vessels/operations have actively commenced clearing the Strait of Hormuz (US/coalition/third-party) between 2026-06-10 and 2026-07-10.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg/CNBC, or a named US/UK/coalition naval/Pentagon statement carried by TIER1.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Stated intent, vessel positioning, or planning without confirmed commencement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved NO. Clean double miss. (1) The dissolution bill's final (third) reading passed July 17, two days after the July 15 EOD deadline. (2) The election was set for October 27, 2026 — the ambiguity rule explicitly states 'if a fixed date on/after Oct 27 is set, resolve NO.' Netanyahu's government completed Israel's first full four-year Knesset term since 1988. Neither deadline criterion nor date criterion was met.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: Resolved YES via ambiguity rule. The coalition fell to approximately 48 seats (below the 61-seat majority threshold in a 120-seat Knesset) after UTJ and Shas departed over the military conscription exemption dispute — confirmed by Jerusalem Post, Haaretz, NPR. Knesset voted 62-0 to dissolve on July 17, 2026; Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until the October 27 election. The forecast's explicit ambiguity rule — 'If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES' — is satisfied. Neither named indicator (Smotrich departure, Degel HaTorah dissolution motion) triggered; the actual mechanism was UTJ/Shas departure. COLD-START: p_inherited=0.35, p_cold=0.05, gap=30pp. HUMAN REVIEW FLAG: The 62-0 dissolution vote passed with Netanyahu's own participation and no formal no-confidence vote. Human reviewer should confirm whether the ambiguity rule overrides both main criteria (no formal roll-call vote confirmed sub-61 majority; no election date earlier than Oct 27).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran sign a comprehensive final agreement covering nuclear program status, Hormuz freedom of navigation, and the US sanctions framework before EOD August 16, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial issuance. August 16 is the nominal 60-day endpoint of the June 17 MOU roadmap. The MOU collapsed in under three weeks: Iran attacked Hormuz ships July 6-7, Trump declared the truce over July 7, and 13 consecutive nights of US strikes followed through July 24. As of July 26, no ceasefire exists, let alone a comprehensive three-pillar deal. Qatar and Oman mediators are pushing a new ceasefire proposal but Iran rejected an Iraqi-presented US proposal. Base rate: zero comprehensive deals completed in 149 war days despite two ceasefire attempts. p=0.10.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES = a written agreement covering at minimum (a) Iran's nuclear program/IAEA access terms, (b) Hormuz freedom of navigation terms, and (c) US primary sanctions framework is signed by named US and Iranian principals before EOD August 16, 2026, with both sides publicly acknowledging the same document.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1: Reuters, AP, AFP, or official joint statement from US State Department and Iranian MFA.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Joint statements of 'roadmap' or 'progress toward a deal' without a signed text = NO. Partial agreements covering only one or two of the three pillars = NO. Ceasefire only without nuclear/sanctions elements = NO. Agreement announced after EOD August 16 UTC = NO.

forecasts.question: Will the US military announce new offensive airstrikes against targets on Iranian territory before EOD July 29, 2026?

Trump's public 'locked and loaded' statement and a senior administration official's characterization of the pause as leverage — designed to show Iran what will happen if they fail to come to the table in a serious way — describe a leverage posture, not a cessation. No mutual ceasefire acknowledgment exists. Prior strike-sequence pattern: each operational pause in this conflict lasted 1-3 days before resumption. p=0.70.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES = CENTCOM or US DoD officially announces airstrikes conducted against targets on Iranian territory between 2026-07-26 and EOD 2026-07-29 (UTC).
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1: CENTCOM official statement, Reuters, AP, NYT, or Washington Post.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: US strikes against Houthi targets, Saudi targets, or non-Iranian territory = NO. US defensive intercepts of Iranian missiles = NO. Strikes against Iranian proxy forces outside Iranian territory = NO. Only confirmed offensive action on Iranian sovereign territory qualifies.

forecasts.question: Will Mojtaba Khamenei deliver a live, verifiably authenticated speech in his role as Supreme Leader of Iran before EOD September 15, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial issuance. Four months of Supreme Leader absence from live audio/video since March 8, 2026 succession. Sole confirmed public appearance was physically masked, voiceless at the July 10-11 memorial for Ali Khamenei. PressTV and IRNA have issued only written statements from the Office of the Supreme Leader and archived footage. Ali Khamenei 40-day memorial (approximately August 17-18) is a potential forcing event. 51-day window allows time for a staged first appearance. Base rate: zero live authenticated speeches in 140+ days as Supreme Leader. p=0.30.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES = Mojtaba Khamenei delivers a live or clearly live-recorded audio or video speech in which his voice is authenticated and he is identified in his Supreme Leader role, confirmed by at least two independent TIER1 sources before EOD September 15, 2026.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1: Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC, Al Jazeera. Sources must confirm live/current attribution, not archived footage.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Masked physical appearance without authenticated audio = NO. Written statements from the Office of the Supreme Leader = NO. Archival footage misidentified as current = NO. Unverified social media clips = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A speech delivered after EOD September 15 UTC = NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Strait of Hormuz 7-day rolling average commercial transit reach at least 25 vessels/day before EOD September 30, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial issuance. IMF PortWatch July 19 (latest published): 15 commercial transits/day — 17% of pre-crisis baseline of approximately 88/day. Lloyd's List July 21: 70% of transits AIS-dark, up from 55% prior week. Inbound Gulf traffic fell to 8 vessels in the most recent 7-day window. Reaching 25/day within 66 days requires a sustained ceasefire, partial AIS transparency restoration, and MCM progress — each necessary but not individually sufficient. Peak following the June 17 MOU reached approximately 25/day briefly before collapsing. p=0.25.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: AIS-dark transits not independently verified by a second OSINT source = excluded from the count. Military vessel transits = excluded. Average must be computed over a rolling 7-day window, not a single-day spike.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran agree to a new formal ceasefire before EOD August 15, 2026?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial issuance. Qatar and Oman submitted a fresh ceasefire proposal on July 21 (Axios). Iran rejected an Iraqi-presented US proposal July 21-25. Trump characterized the July 25 pause as leverage. Both sides are managing the strike/pause cycle ahead of the August 16 MOU 60-day deadline. Pattern: each prior ceasefire was announced within 48-72 hours of an operational pause; July 25 marks day 1 of the current pause. Frequency base rate: two formal ceasefires in 149 days (~1 per 75 days); at 20 days remaining that implies ~27% frequency-alone base rate, adjusted to 0.35 for the fresh mediator proposal and approaching focal-point deadline. p=0.35.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES = Both US and Iranian governments publicly acknowledge the same ceasefire through official statements agreeing to halt active offensive military strikes against each other's territory for a defined period, before EOD August 15, 2026.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1: Reuters, AP, AFP. Must confirm both sides' acknowledgment using each side's own official communications. Mediator announcement alone without US and Iranian confirmation = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral pause by one side without mutual acknowledgment = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Informal operational pause without official acknowledgment from both sides = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Ceasefire covering only proxy forces without covering direct US-Iran exchanges = NO. Ceasefire formally agreed before deadline but subsequently violated = still YES if the agreement was reached before EOD August 15.
